findings.published: Who this is for: This is for the low-serotonin-looking pattern, not for every depressed person.
findings.why: "either" points back to something that isn't in this passage, so a reader starting at this section has to guess what else was "not for every depressed person".

findings.now: It could help, though, with a low-serotonin-looking pattern, where it's hard to fall asleep and your mood is low, without much warmth to it.
findings.published: Think poor sleep initiation, low mood, low warmth, night anxiety, repetitive rumination, and a genetic or clinical reason to suspect a bottleneck in serotonin synthesis.
findings.why: "without much warmth to it" makes warmth a quality of the mood, where PUBLISHED listed low warmth as a sign of its own, and a reader has to guess what a mood "without much warmth to it" is.
where: Serotonin Bottleneck Pattern: 5-HTP + Low-Dose P5P (two of its paragraphs, as they would read), P1

findings.now: It makes more sense if there's also a genetic or clinical reason to suspect a bottleneck in serotonin synthesis, like with Scott, whose genetic data pointed to a TPH2 bottleneck, and 5-HTP helped his sleep and mood.
findings.published: Think poor sleep initiation, low mood, low warmth, night anxiety, repetitive rumination, and a genetic or clinical reason to suspect a bottleneck in serotonin synthesis. Scott’s genetic data suggested a TPH2 bottleneck, and 5-HTP helped his sleep and mood.
findings.why: PUBLISHED made the genetic or clinical reason part of the pattern ("and"), while NOW makes it an optional extra ("makes more sense if there's also"), and "It" could be the pattern or taking 5-HTP.

findings.now: I'd avoid casually experimenting with 5-HTP if you're agitated or manic, as it could sometimes push that further. And don't take it with anything else that raises serotonin, like most antidepressants or MDMA, since together they can cause serotonin syndrome, a dangerous overload of serotonin (the warnings at the top list those drugs).
findings.published: If you are already agitated, manic, on serotonergic meds, or using serotonergic psychedelics/entactogens, this is not a casual experiment.
findings.why: PUBLISHED named serotonergic psychedelics among the cases where this is "not a casual experiment"; NOW names only antidepressants and MDMA, turns "not casual" into a flat "don't" for those, and leaves a psychedelic user unsure whether psychedelics count as something "that raises serotonin" (the next paragraph then says mushrooms are up to you).
where: Serotonin Bottleneck Pattern: 5-HTP + Low-Dose P5P (two of its paragraphs, as they would read), P1

findings.now: If you're doing psychedelics, be especially strict around ayahuasca's harmala MAOI chemistry and around iboga or ibogaine: never take 5-HTP on the same day as ayahuasca or iboga, though it's fine the day before, or the day after ayahuasca.
findings.published: If you're doing psychedelics, avoid 5-HTP on the same day as a trip, and be especially strict around ayahuasca's harmala MAOI chemistry and around iboga or ibogaine.
findings.why: The general rule (no 5-HTP on the day of any trip) is gone, so "especially strict" has nothing to be stricter than and a reader taking LSD, or a full dose of anything not named, gets no instruction.
where: Serotonin Bottleneck Pattern: 5-HTP + Low-Dose P5P (two of its paragraphs, as they would read), P2

findings.now: never take 5-HTP on the same day as ayahuasca or iboga, though it's fine the day before, or the day after ayahuasca.
findings.why: A reader has to reread to work out that "the day before" covers both and "the day after" only ayahuasca; it can also be read as "the day before or the day after, for ayahuasca only", which leaves the day before iboga open.
where: Serotonin Bottleneck Pattern: 5-HTP + Low-Dose P5P (two of its paragraphs, as they would read), P2

findings.now: After a low dose of iboga, wait a day, and after a bigger dose usually a few days. After a flood dose (one big dose), people often wait weeks before taking anything psychoactive, mainly so they don't block the after-effects they took iboga for. While you're microdosing iboga, leave 5-HTP out altogether.
findings.why: Four dose sizes come one after another ("low dose", "bigger dose", "flood dose (one big dose)", "microdosing") with "bigger" and "one big" easy to mix up and no word on how a low dose (wait a day) differs from a microdose (leave it out altogether).
where: Serotonin Bottleneck Pattern: 5-HTP + Low-Dose P5P (two of its paragraphs, as they would read), P2

findings.now: With mushrooms, it's up to you whether to take 5-HTP, and I don't think it should be a problem with this protocol's mushroom microdoses.
findings.published: If you're doing psychedelics, avoid 5-HTP on the same day as a trip, and be especially strict around ayahuasca's harmala MAOI chemistry and around iboga or ibogaine.
findings.why: PUBLISHED said to avoid 5-HTP on the day of a trip, and NOW says "it's up to you" without saying it means the same day or whether that covers a full mushroom trip as well as the microdoses, which also sits oddly after the previous paragraph's "don't take it with anything else that raises serotonin".
where: Serotonin Bottleneck Pattern: 5-HTP + Low-Dose P5P (two of its paragraphs, as they would read), P2
